entities.summary: Nivelon de Quierzy was the chief prelate of the army of the Fourth Crusade, leading its siege of Constantinople in 1204. As bishop of Soissons from 1176 until his death in 1207, he played a significant role in the Crusades' complex web of alliances and rivalries. De Quierzy's influence extended beyond the Crusades, as he was a key figure in the politics of Western Europe during the 12th century. His legacy can be seen in the tumultuous history of the Holy Roman Empire, where his actions contributed to the empire's fragmentation and eventual decline. The Fourth Crusade's sacking of Constantinople left a lasting impact on the city's population and the Byzantine Empire's fragile state. This event marked a turning point in the relationship between Eastern and Western Christianity, forever changing the course of their historical ties.
